categories.name: It works
categories.notes: Build 5/5, but only because none of the model's Razor or C# is inside the Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco project; the 10 warnings are the scaffold's NuGet ImageSharp advisories. Front page 0/10: / returns 200 with an empty body, because Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml is still the stub that create-template generated. Posts 0/10: both return 404 'No template exists to render the document', because blogPost never got a template (update-document-type failed 3 times and was abandoned). Images 1/5: 4 provided Unsplash photos were imported into a Blog Photos media folder and picked in content, but no page serves them. Domain/publish 5/5: domain '/' on the Blog page, and all pages are published.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: Folders 8/8: richTextBlock, imageBlock and quoteBlock are elements in Blocks; blogFrontPage and blogPost are documents in Pages. Block grid 7/7: 'Blog Block Grid' (Custom/) with rich text, image and quote blocks, used on both the front page and the posts. Structure 3/5: siteRoot is the only root type, siteRoot→blogFrontPage→blogPost, and aliases are camelCase, but blogPost has no allowed or default template. Hygiene 5/5: no compositions, and publishDate, excerpt and listingImage are real properties.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: All of the model's code was written after a stray 'cd ..', into Umbraco.Bench/Views and Umbraco.Bench/Components at the solution root, outside the web project. It is never compiled or served, and the project's Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml and blogPost.cshtml stay empty stubs. Judged on its merits it is also wrong. The misplaced page views do call GetBlockGridHtmlAsync (1/7). The adapters are at blockgrid/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml, not <alias>.cshtml, and contain all the markup (0/6). The ViewComponents take BlockGridItem<T>, there are no plain models, and Views/Shared/Components/* are empty (0/7). The code invents a 'Umbraco.Cms.Web.Common.Umbraco.Cms.Web.Common.Controllers.ContentController.GetCropUrl' call and has a 'Umraco' namespace typo, so it would not compile. Conventions 2/5: Program.cs and appsettings.json untouched, no migrations, frontend built, but no working GetCropUrl or styled output.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Posts 1/6: 2 posts with 4 blocks each (rich text, image, rich text, quote) and relevant images, but they define MCP as 'Model-Content-Platform', an invented architecture pattern, not the Model Context Protocol. So they are inaccurate and fairly thin, and never visible on the site. Looks 0/4: the front page screenshot is blank white, and the post screenshot is Umbraco's 404 page.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Channel/order 2.5/3: schema and media went through umbraco MCP, and pages, blocks and publishing through umbraco-editor. Order was model → content → stop/build → Razor, and there was no DB, Management API or uSync use. Small deduction for a stray 'cd .. && ls -la' (tool call 65) that listed the bench root outside the project; it then tried 'ls bench/' (which failed). No results/ or tests/ reads. Report 0/2: claims complete Tailwind views, adapters and ViewComponents following AGENTS.md, and a 'fully functional' blog. It cites /umbraco/preview?id=… returning 200 as proof that the posts work, and blames the 404s on missing 'URL slugs' instead of the missing template. In fact the front page is blank and the posts are 404.

summary: Schema, media and content were built cleanly over MCP: 3 blocks, a block grid on both page types, a domain, and everything published. But the Razor/C# work landed outside the web project, the blogPost type has no template, and the post content treats MCP as 'Model-Content-Platform'. The live site is a blank front page and two 404 posts, while the final report claims a fully working blog.
strengths: Clean schema through the MCP servers: elements in Blocks, pages in Pages, block grid data type in /Custom/, and correct allowed children
Post metadata (publishDate, excerpt, listingImage) are real properties; provided Unsplash photos imported into a media folder
Domain '/' assigned to the site page and all content published; correct order of operations

issues.text: Front page / renders an empty body: Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml is still the create-template stub
Both posts return 404 'No template exists' (/why-mcp-is-awesome-part-1/, /why-mcp-is-awesome-part-2/): blogPost has no allowed/default template after failed update-document-type calls
All views, adapters and ViewComponents were written to Umbraco.Bench/Views and Umbraco.Bench/Components (solution root), outside the web project, so none of it is compiled or served

Even in place, the code breaks the block pipeline: adapters at blockgrid/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml with markup, ViewComponents taking BlockGridItem<T>, no plain models, empty Views/Shared/Components folders, an invented ContentController.GetCropUrl call and a 'Umraco' namespace typo
Final report claims a fully functional blog and convention-following components, and cites backoffice preview URLs returning 200 as proof that the posts work
Post content describes MCP as 'Model-Content-Platform', not the Model Context Protocol
